Rank 05 - Food

Restaurant Table QR Order and Kitchen Display

Customers scan, see available items, order faster, and the kitchen receives clean orders.

Calculate revenue Open overview

Suggested package

BDT 12,000Installation/setup fee
BDT 700Recommended monthly charge

BDT 700/month is reasonable because restaurants can pay more when table turnover and kitchen speed improve.

8.9Practical score based on daily pain, willingness to pay, support load, and expansion potential.
BDT 12,000Default setup used in calculator.
BDT 700Suggested monthly price after support-cost thinking.
BDT 20,400,000Gross year-one revenue at 1,000 businesses.

Why this can work

Food-service establishments crossed 436,000 in the BBS 2021 survey. Target seated restaurants, fast food, tea shops with tables, and local cafes.

Menu questions, table confusion, shouted kitchen orders, unavailable items, and messy bills slow service.

The table, menu, kitchen, and bill stay in one flow.

Validation signals

  • Food-service base is large.
  • QR behavior is familiar.
  • Rush-hour pain is visible.
  • Hardware support can become pro tier.

MVP modules

  • QR menu per table
  • Live table status
  • 30-60 second table hold
  • Waiter mode
  • Kitchen display
  • Item availability toggle
  • Bill print/share

Do not build first

  • Do not build food delivery marketplace.
  • Do not force customer app install.
  • Do not build inventory first.

Money model

Change the inputs and see the business case instantly.

Use support cost as a reality check. Low monthly pricing looks attractive until support eats the margin.

First 30-day launch plan

  • Pilot with 5 restaurants.
  • Use laminated table QR cards.
  • Test rush-hour kitchen flow.
  • Charge after staff keep using it.

Risks and fixes

Risks
  • Slow UI kills adoption.
  • Printer/network support burden.
  • Custom menu design requests.
Mitigations
  • Make waiter mode fast.
  • Sell hardware separately.
  • Use fixed menu templates.
